d: Boarding a train at Neelavalley, the weight of trauma around broke her completely — she collapsed, and didn’t move for hours. What came after wasn’t recovery. It was a calling: visions, symbols, a framework older than her understanding of herself, surfacing not as myth but as mechanism.
kit: TRISHULA · TRIKALA DRISHTI · RUDRAKSHA MALA · DAMRU

d: A soldier un-made from his wrath and rebuilt around compassion. Living proof of the framework’s promise.
kit: A reclaimed Trishulvane trident-tool; close-guard combat; the ability to physically hold a space stable while Rudrakshi runs a scan inside it.

powers.lore: He does not raise his weapon first. Once cold-world muscle, built to break rather than hold — Rudrakshi found him, beaded him, turned him. Now he plants Trishulvane into wet stone and holds an entire space steady while a healer works inside it. No wound opens twice on his watch.

ordinaryLife.lore: Off duty, that same restraint gets complicated. Worst person to bring on a grocery run — treats it like a perimeter sweep, insists on walking half a step ahead "out of habit." Cannot dance, has never admitted this. Reorganizes other people's kitchens out of nervous energy and has never once successfully explained why.

d: Fire-speech. The warm world’s morale, news, and counter-propaganda all move on this frequency.
kit: Damru-based sound-tech that carries ETH-attuned frequencies across a whole city; the ability to steady a crowd’s collective grief through sound alone.

powers.lore: Every city needs a voice it trusts. Neelavalley has Agnivaak. He broadcasts from the top of Trispire, where his ETH-etched damru carries further than any signal tower could manage alone — one strike, and the frequency moves through a thousand rooftops at once. Grief steadies. Fear settles. He is not a fighter. His weapon is presence.

ordinaryLife.lore: Chronically, almost heroically late to everything that isn't a scheduled transmission. Hums constantly, unconsciously — the rest of the cast can read his mood from the tune before he's said a word. Genuinely terrible at small talk one-on-one; all that easy charisma switches off the second the crowd disappears.

d: Keeper of the oldest ETH cores. Reached total containment decades ago — and chose to maintain rather than heal.
kit: Mastery of the Kailasa Samhita meditative operating system; hand-built ETH cores; the still-point discipline that lets a healer hold without leaking.

powers.lore: The elder ascetic-engineer who maintains the ETH core doesn't move to fix what's broken. He steadies his breath, and the framework steadies with him — no visible burst, no dramatic display. Just the quiet, absolute stillness of someone who stopped needing to perform urgency decades ago. This is what discipline looks like when it's finally finished proving itself.

ordinaryLife.lore: Spends more time than anyone will admit reorganizing the archive shelves by a system nobody else understands. Has strong, unspoken opinions about which oil-lantern wicks burn cleanest. Has been quietly awake before every single person in Vedavale for as long as anyone can remember — nobody's ever actually seen him sleep.

d: Reads what could be. Has seen your worst future before you’ve lived it — invaluable, and slightly feared.
kit: Moon-attuned navigation through the Chandravault; the ability to walk a target’s possible futures before the scan begins; soma-linked dream-work.

powers.lore: Not every healer reads what is. Some read what could be. Chandrahollis walks a target's possible futures before her scan even begins — moon-attuned, dream-linked, invaluable and slightly feared in equal measure. That kind of sight comes with a cost nobody talks about: she carries other people's worst futures without always being able to warn them.

ordinaryLife.lore: The Academy's dream-walker is a genuinely terrible sleeper — insomnia, most nights. Drifts mid-conversation, three futures deep into a boring meeting, and has gotten very good at nodding at exactly the right moment to cover for it. Never play cards with her.

d: The first fully Academy-raised pure soul. The gift without the wound; the sight without the scar.
kit: Natural three-ring sight from childhood; the fastest scan in the Academy; untested containment — she has never yet had to hold real poison.

powers.lore: She has the gift without the wound. Sharavinka is the Academy's first fully raised "pure soul" — the fastest scan in the Academy, full three-ring vision before she was old enough to fully understand what it meant. Here's the flaw: she's never had to hold real poison. Never been burned by what she contains.

ordinaryLife.lore: Has never once walked into a room without scanning it out of habit — including her own kitchen, including a mirror, for a full ten seconds. Startle her and the scan-rings flare on reflex, usually followed by knocking something over. The senior cast has started leaving breakable things out of arm's reach.

d: No powers — languages, contacts, safe-routes, and trust on both sides of the seam.
kit: No powers to speak of — pure human craft: languages, contacts, safe-routes, and the trust of people on both sides. Knows Antaryana better than anyone.

powers.lore: No glowing rings. No third eye. No circuit-lines. Ziaraka's only power is craft — languages, contacts, safe-routes, and trust earned on both sides of a border most people are too afraid to stand in. She's the one warm-world character genuinely comfortable in the seam between worlds, because she's spent years learning it isn't a line to fight over. It's just a place, if you know how to move through it.

ordinaryLife.lore: Owns exactly one bag and has never once misplaced anything in it, which the rest of the cast finds deeply unsettling. Can haggle in four languages and has strong opinions about which border-market stall oversells its spice-lanterns. Has slept in more borrowed beds than anyone in this universe and still somehow always knows exactly where she is.

d: Twitchy street runner; knows every warm back-lane and every debt owed on it.
kit: Every warm-world back-lane committed to memory, and a running ledger of who owes what on each of them.

d: Half-broken empath; reads the emotional static of a crowd. Useful and unstable.
kit: Reads the emotional static of a crowd and calls a mood before it turns — unreliable at range, worse under pressure.

d: Deals in the fiercer rumours — the ones that touch the border and Bhairava’s edge.
kit: A rumour-network reaching the border and Bhairava’s edge; carries the fiercer intel nobody else will touch.
